summary: This article explains how moving plates fold rock into mountains, how lava builds volcanoes, and how erosion slowly wears mountains down.
introduce: Show the title “How Mountains Grow” and give pairs one minute to predict, in one sentence, what the whole article is mostly about. Write three predictions on the board and tell students they will check which one is closest to the main idea after reading.

keyTerms.def: the very top of a mountain
the remains or marks of very old living things kept in rock

challengeTerms.def: having to do with the huge moving plates of the Earth's crust
to press something together so it takes up less space
the slow raising of land to a higher level

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that mountains never change? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Mount Everest is growing taller, but erosion is also wearing it down.
struggling: Pre-teach collide, summit, and fossils with pictures or gestures, then let weak readers complete a main-idea-and-details web with a partner.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses tectonic, compress, and uplift to state the main idea of the article in their own words.
